text:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing a spike in GPU join failures in eu-west-1 starting ~09:11 UTC, lots of KMS Decrypt denied errors in keystore-proxy logs
ashok: yikes, alerted me too. dashboard: https://grafana.company/internal/d/alerts/gpu-joins-eu ? :eyes:
sre-bot: Alert: region=eu-west-1 metric=gpu_node_join_fail rate=14m threshold=8m (fired at 09:12 UTC)
jordan: any recent infra changes in that region? firewall, ACLs, nat routing?
maria: infra rolled a privnet ACL tighten at 09:05 to make ephemeral proxy outbound default-deny (part of lockdown change)
jordan: that would break keystore access — warm-pool nodes reach keystore via ephemeral outbound from warm-subnets to keystore-proxy. If egress blocked, KMS decrypts fail
leah: can we see a sample error from a joining node to confirm it's kms:Decrypt AccessDenied and not cert/trust issue?
maria: paste from node gpu-01: ```
2026-03-21T09:11:32Z ERROR keystore: decrypt failed client=gpu-01 DecryptError AccessDenied: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:111222333:key/abcd-ef01
CausedBy: network deny from 10.3.8.21:56312
```
ashok: yep network deny. quick options: 1) rollback the ACL (fastest), 2) add temporary allow from warm-pool CIDR to keystore-proxy:443 TTL, 3) punch through via a different NAT path. Rollback is fastest but might conflict with broader lockdown deploy
jordan: suggest temp allow rule with short TTL + audit tag, avoids full rollback risk. I'll prepare a targeted TF change: `terraform apply -target=module.firewall.rule.temporary_keystore_allow`
maria: infra ops: would approve temporary allow for 30m with audit tag `incident=keystore-egress-eu`
leah: security ok with that for emergency, but require increasing keystore audit sampling to 100% during window and capturing all decrypt failures for forensic review
sre-bot: Playbook recommended: `emergency-egress-exception` -> create allow rule -> ramp audit sampling -> restart warmup agents -> monitor joins. playbook: https://playbooks.company/egress-exception
jordan: applying rule now. plan shows +1 rule, allow src=10.3.8.0/24 dest=keystore-proxy.eu-west-1.svc:443 TTL=1800s tag=incident=keystore-egress-eu id=tf-ephem-1234
sre-bot: Change detected: tf-ephem-1234 applied by jordan at 09:17 UTC. New rule created with TTL=1800s
maria: triggering a daemonset restart to re-attempt joins: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/gpu-warmup`
ashok: keystore audit sampling bumped to 100% at 09:18 UTC (audit-id=AUD-9831)
jordan: seeing first decrypt successes on gpu-01 at 09:18:46, join rate improved from ~3/min to ~15/min
maria: joining stabilized in the last 6m. keystore decrypt 403s dropped from ~220/min to ~7/min :white_check_mark:
leah: good containment. follow-ups: (1) record ACL diff and TF change in incident ticket, (2) harden firewall templates so future default-deny deploys check warm-pool feature flag, (3) scope allow to service-account IPs rather than entire subnet if possible
jordan: will open infra PR to add predeploy check and to make allow target service endpoint FQDN+SA instead of CIDR. also remove TTL extension from template to avoid accidental permanent allow
maria: creating incident INC-2026-0422 and attaching logs, tf change id tf-ephem-1234, audit-id AUD-9831
ashok: note: there was a small cost bump due to node churn during rejoin (~$120 extra for EU warm pool churn) — will include in postmortem
leah: compliance note: update runbook with an approved emergency-exception flow requiring security+infra+oncall sign-off and mandating full audit capture during exception windows
sre-bot: Tentative resolution: keystore egress allow applied at 09:17 UTC, validation shows normal join rates at 09:20 UTC. Monitor 30m for regressions
maria: confirmed stable at 09:35 UTC, closing incident for now. PM/infra/security to coordinate postmortem and remediation by EOD :memo:
